DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord due to Vitamin B12 deficiency.

The rapid onset of neurological deficits (1-week) combined with cognitive changes and gait instability in a 44-year-old male is highly suggestive of B12 deficiency, particularly given the involvement of both the dorsal columns (ataxia, unsteadiness) and lateral corticospinal tracts (weakness, falls), alongside potential psychiatric manifestations like paranoia.

REQUEST TEST: Serum Vitamin B12, Methylmalonic Acid (MMA), and Homocysteine levels.
